# Passing Parameters

A very simple application that reads the command line arguments and properties
(prefixed `app.`) passed to the application.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── passing-parameters.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the JAR file contents

   ```shell
   jar --list --file='./target/libs/passing-parameters.jar' | sort
   ```

   The application JAR file contents

   ```
   demo/
   demo/Main.class
   META-INF/
   META-INF/MANIFEST.MF
   META-INF/maven/
   META-INF/maven/demo/
   META-INF/maven/demo/passing-parameters/
   META-INF/maven/demo/passing-parameters/pom.properties
   META-INF/maven/demo/passing-parameters/pom.xml
   module-info.class
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

3. Describe the JAR file

   Describe the `passing-parameters.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/passing-parameters.jar'
   ```

   The passing-parameters module description

   ```
   demo@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/passing-parameters.jar!/module-info.class
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo
   main-class demo.Main
   ```

   Note that the module’s main class is defined, thus we can run the application
   without providing the main class canonical path.

   The main class is defined in the `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file that was created
   by maven.

   ```shell
   unzip -p './target/libs/passing-parameters.jar' 'META-INF/MANIFEST.MF'
   ```

   This will print the contents of the manifest file

   ```
   Manifest-Version: 1.0
   Created-By: Maven JAR Plugin 3.5.1
   Java-Version: 25
   Build-Jdk-Spec: 25
   Main-Class: demo.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   Run the application using the class path (`-jar`)

   ```shell
   java \
     -Dapp.name='Passing Parameters' \
     -Dapp.version=1 \
     -jar './target/libs/passing-parameters.jar' \
     'Hello world' \
     '12345'
   ```

   The application will run and print the following

   ```
   Has 2 properties (that starts with 'app.')
    - [app.version] '1'
    - [app.name] 'Passing Parameters'
   Received 2 parameters
    - [0] 'Hello world'
    - [1] '12345'
   ```

   Run the application using the class path (`--class-path`)

   ```shell
   java \
     -Dapp.name='Passing Parameters' \
     -Dapp.version=1 \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main \
     'Hello world' \
     '12345'
   ```

   The application will run and print the following

   ```
   Has 2 properties (that starts with 'app.')
    - [app.version] '1'
    - [app.name] 'Passing Parameters'
   Received 2 parameters
    - [0] 'Hello world'
    - [1] '12345'
   ```

   Run the application using the module path (`--module-path`)

   ```shell
   java \
     -Dapp.name='Passing Parameters' \
     -Dapp.version=1 \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo \
     'Hello world' \
     '12345'
   ```

   The application will run and print the following

   ```
   Has 2 properties (that starts with 'app.')
    - [app.version] '1'
    - [app.name] 'Passing Parameters'
   Received 2 parameters
    - [0] 'Hello world'
    - [1] '12345'
   ```
